articleTitle: Development of AI Vision Inspection System for UAV Imagery Surveillance of Transmission Towers
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: High-voltage transmission line networks are essential for electricity delivery and require proactive maintenance to prevent breakdowns due to steady demand and full-capacity operation. Federal and state regulations require annual inspections of the right-of-way (ROW) and transmission infrastructure. Traditionally, helicopters are used for these inspections, but they are costly. Another issue is that power outages and financial losses are still caused by vegetation encroachment in power line corridors. To address this, we propose an automated method combining robotics, photogrammetry, and computer vision. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) present a viable monitoring alternative because of their speedy and cost-effective high-resolution image capturing. However, segmenting vegetation encroachment in these images is difficult due to the complexity and pixel imbalance. We propose a deep learning-based approach to address these challenges by dividing the dataset into 3 classes: power line, background, and vegetation. Using the UAV- VEPL-NET dataset and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model, initial training will be conducted with the help of Roboflow software. This approach will help the system detect with high accuracy. The final model will then be embedded into the UAV for testing. Overall, the average precision of the demo training in Roboflow was 93%, whereas the accuracy for every class was 93% for the power line, 89% for the background, and 96% for the vegetation.

articleTitle: Dielectric Resonator-Based MIMO Antenna With Pattern Diversity for 5G Millimeter-Wave Application
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: This study presents a quad-port, box-shaped multiple-input-multiple-output cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (CDRA) that exhibits quad-directional pattern diversity for new radio frequency bands named n260 under the 5G millimeter-wave communication. The antenna operates between 36.30 GHz to 40.60 GHz frequency range. The primary structure consists of a CDRA excited with the help of a rectangular aperture and a modified microstrip feed line. This structure is replicated and arranged in a box configuration, resulting in a quad-port MIMO antenna system. The DRA elements are placed so that their adjacent broad-side radiation patterns are 90 degrees apart from each other in an azimuthal direction, providing a spatially decoupled radiation pattern and resulting in enhanced isolation. The proposed MIMO antenna achieves over 30 dB of isolation between antenna ports without additional decoupling structures. This structure is suitable for 5G new radio frequency bands n260 under millimeter-wave communication, forthcoming communication and IoT applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of Gait Impairment Features for Post-Stroke Patients Using Principal Component Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Stroke is a life-altering disease that can affect any individual and many of them experience different degrees of gait impairment. Thus, an individualistic approach is required in aiding the post-stroke patient with their gait rehabilitation. However, such an approach is still lacking in Malaysia. Hence, for this research, the relevant gait features were identified and gait analysis was implemented to understand how much a gait feature contributed to the gait impairment among post-stroke patients using the unsupervised machine learning approach. The gait features were obtained using the G-Walk Gait Analysis System. The Principal Component Analysis (PCA) method was utilized to identify how much a gait feature contributed to the gait impairment. After implementing PCA, the first four principal components with a cumulative contribution rate of 82.59% were utilized to figure out the gait features that have the highest loading factors. From the analysis, it was found out that temporal, spatial, propulsion and pelvis kinematic features contributed to the patient's gait impairment as these features made up the highest or one of the highest loading factors in the first four PCs.

articleTitle: Towards Efficient Gait Analysis Using Gyroscope: Preliminary Results and Insights
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Wearable sensor technology, combined with smartphone capabilities, has become a powerful and costeffective solution for gait analysis, offering real-time monitoring of human movements. This study introduces a sensor-based gait event detection system using gyroscope data from the publicly available MotionSense dataset to analyze walking and jogging. The dataset, which includes six subjects of varying demographics, provides a broader understanding of gait patterns. Gyroscope data from the X-axis was used to detect key biomechanical events, such as heel strikes, toe-offs, and mid-swings, as these align with the sagittal plane and are critical in understanding walking dynamics. The gait event detection algorithm The detection algorithm, developed in Python, incorporates advanced signal processing techniques like the Savitzky-Golay filter, to reduce noise while preserving key data. By using a threshold-based and sliding window methods, the system identifies gait events accurately and calculates key gait parameters such as cadence, stance time, swing time, and phase distributions. The results show significant differences between walking and jogging, with jogging exhibiting a higher cadence (82.71-90.23 steps/min) and shorter stance times (0.37-0.46 seconds) compared to walking (52.63-60.15 steps/min, stance time 0.61-0.85 seconds). This research demonstrates that wearable sensor technology offers precise and scalable alternatives to expensive, complex traditional gait analysis systems. The findings show the system's potential for clinical monitoring, rehabilitation, sports science, and smart wearable device development.

articleTitle: Water Quality Monitoring for Catfish Biofloc Using Fuzzy Decision
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Catfish (Clarias gariepinus) farming is one of the rapidly growing fisheries sectors and has great potential to fulfill the increased demand for fish consumption. Water quality has a significant influence on the survival, growth, and production rate of catfish. Currently, water quality monitoring is still done manually by visiting each pond, which requires a lot of time and energy, and the monitoring results are less accurate. This research develops and implements an Internet of Things (IoT)-based water quality monitoring system that can monitor parameters such as pH, temperature, and water turbidity in real time by taking data twice an hour. This system uses the Mamdani fuzzy method to determine the water quality status. The results show that the Mamdani fuzzy method has a 100% accuracy rate based on ideal water quality status ranges pH level between 6.5 – 8.5, temperature between 25 – 30°C, and turbidity between 0 – 50 NTU consistently. In addition, the system uses a database to monitor trends in water quality changes, with results showing that the sensor technology in this system improves the efficiency and sustainability of catfish farming. The application of technology in water quality monitoring is essential to ensure the environmental health of fish and the sustainability of the fisheries sector.

articleTitle: Multiwavelength Fiber Laser Based on Different Combinations of Dual-Bidirectional SOAs Incorporating a Lyot Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: We demonstrated dual-bidirectional semiconductor optical amplifiers (SOAs) based on Lyot filters. Two combinations of SOAs are investigated; non-linear SOA (NLSOA) and linear SOA (LSOA) as well as NLSOA and booster SOA (BOA). The spectrum of multiwavelength fiber laser from NLSOA-LSOA generated higher lasing lines and extinction ratio as compared to NLSOA-BOA. The variation of SOA current shows different lasing lines and multiwavelength flatness. Changing the polarization state on polarization controllers (PCs) improperly seems to deteriorate the multiwavelength spectrum due to a weaker intensity-dependent loss strength and degradation of constructive interference of the Lyot filter. The nonlinear polarization rotation (NPR) effect resulted in optimal performance with a flat multiwavelength spectrum, highlighting the need for optimized polarization control.

articleTitle: A 6.78-MHz Free-Positioning Wireless Charging Bowl with Optimized Passive Electromagnetic Shield for Wearable Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: This paper presents a wireless charging bowl with a double-layer electromagnetic shield comprising a magnetic layer and a conductive layer to reduce the leakage magnetic field. A complete parametric analysis of the wireless power transfer (WPT) system with the double-layer shield structure is performed using Ansys High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS) software. The simulation results show that the quality factor of the transmitter (Tx) is effectively improved by increasing the gap between the shield and the Tx, while the shielding characteristic is preserved. An optimal gap of 5 mm is selected to achieve a balance between the system performance and the Tx size. The measured maximum power transfer efficiency (PTE) of the WPT system with the proposed Tx decreases only 3.5%, from 95 % to 91.5%, when applying the double-layer shield with an optimal gap of 5 mm, while the leakage magnetic field is reduced by 98%.

articleTitle: Study on Morphological and Wettability Characteristics of Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) for Human Skin Mimicking Phantom
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: A phantom is a model that mimics human tissue or part of a human body. It has been widely used due to its advantages in biomedical applications for studying human morphology, device testing, and diagnosis. However, human characteristics are complex, and researchers still find it challenging to mimic more than one characteristic in the phantom. The skin is the primary external barrier that covers the entire human body, and the structure of the skin layer is characterized by its unique features. This study fabricates a skin phantom (SP) by using polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) as the tissue mimicking material (TMM) to study morphological and wettability. Aluminum oxide (AI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) and India ink were added with three different formulations (SP 1, SP 2, SP3) to increase their characteristics. By using the mold-casting technique during fabrication, the skin surface texture morphology was imitated. The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images showed the valley and plateaus of the skin with measurements of the lowest valleys (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${R_{v}}$</tex> = −51.178μm), highest peak (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${R_{p}}$</tex> = 87.354μm), and surface roughness (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${R_{q}}$</tex> = 13.525μm). The wettability showed an increment of hydrophobic behavior with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\theta_{PDMS}}$</tex> = 93.20°, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\theta_{SP1}}$</tex> = 102.90°, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\theta_{SP2}}$</tex> = 103.80°, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\theta_{SP3}}$</tex> = 104.40°. Thus, the skin phantom has shown morphology and wettability characteristics, and has the potential to be utilized for device testing and diagnosis

articleTitle: Simulation of Bare Coreless Silica Fiber Sensor for Humidity Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Coreless silica fiber (CSF) has attracted significant interest for its application in humidity sensing, particularly when utilizing hygroscopic thin films or coatings as humidity-sensitive materials. However, the inherent limitations of these materials complicate the fabrication process of CSF-based humidity sensors, leading to increased costs and introducing substantial cross-sensitivity to temperature. In response, this paper introduces a simulation of a bare CSF design aimed at humidity sensing. We evaluated the sensor's performance by simulating various humidity levels through adjustments in the analyte's refractive index, ranging from 1.000 RIU (0 %RH) to 1.333 RIU (100 %RH). The results indicate that the bare or uncoated CSF design successfully detects humidity changes (1.00 to 1.333 RI), achieving a sensitivity of 1.319 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−9</sup> RIU per unit of RI change and demonstrating strong linearity with an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>value of 0.9468. Additionally, decreasing the diameter of the CSF significantly increases the sensor's sensitivity. These results lay the groundwork for future experimental work on fiber humidity sensors. Moreover, the insights gained from this study may develop smart sensors integrated with IoT systems for real-time environmental monitoring. Such advancements hold promise for enhancing the efficiency and responsiveness of agricultural management and industrial automation systems.

articleTitle: Optimized Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) Antenna for Wearable Health Monitoring Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Around 50 million people in the world are affected by chronic seizures and epilepsy. Seizures are usually diagnosed by CT scans, MRI scans, EEGs, and blood tests. However, there is a need for devices that help people to detect and receive alerts before the onset of a seizure episode. This paper addresses the need to design a seizure detection device that works on the principle of changing muscle permittivity. As chronic seizures can be life-threatening, there is a need for devices that detect seizures before their onset, to help a person take precautionary measures. Though there are a few devices that work for this application, there is always room for improvement and innovation. Therefore, we have proposed a novel microstrip patch antenna that acts as a miniaturised biosensor. One of the major symptoms of seizure is the change in muscle stiffness. Considering this factor, our antenna is designed to detect the change in the permittivity caused due to the change in muscle tension which is reflected through the S parameter graph that gives us the information to detect a seizure attack beforehand. The return loss of the antenna is improved -27.596 dB by introducing the concept of substrate integrated waveguides. The antenna will be integrated into an embedded system design to enable it to function as a wearable device. Also, the SAR properties are analysed and optimized as per the FCC standards as it would be modelled as a wearable device. The antenna has been designed, simulated, and analysed using the ANSYS HFSS tool. Further, a comparative study on the various patch shapes, substrate materials, and SIWs was also made using ANSYS HFSS.

articleTitle: LSTVision: A Multi-Modal Framework for Autism Spectrum Diagnosis Utilizing LSTM and Vision Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a unique neurological condition that is characterized by a variety of intricate challenges in the field of neurodevelopmental disorders. Effectively addressing the impact and reducing the severity of ASD is significantly impeded by the delayed detection of the condition. A thorough examination of the underlying structures and various data types is necessary to address these complexities. The majority of prior research has focused on the use of a single modality form of data to diagnose ASD. Nevertheless, there has been a significant transition toward the use of multimodal frameworks with various techniques, as they can effectively integrate and manage a wide range of data types. This study used the ABIDE I dataset to develop a multimodal ASD framework known as LSTVision. This framework incorporates LSTM for clinical features and a vision transformer for MRI analysis. The final diagnosis output is generated by concatenating the output from the LSTM and vision transformer and forwarding it to the classification network. Our developed LSTVision outperforms with an accuracy of 0.948, as demonstrated by experimental results. Furthermore, a more comprehensive understanding of the innate characteristics of ASD may be achieved by examining brain MRI.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of YOLO Models for Melon Leaf Disease Classification in UAV-Assisted Smart Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: By tackling global issues like population increase and climate change, advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning (DL) are changing the agricultural industry. In order to improve food security and resource sustainability, this study focuses on applying computer vision (CV) and DL approaches to detect diseases in rock melon plants. Disease identification is difficult due to the complexity of plant growth and the variability of environmental variables. Our study uses the most recent YOLOv9 and YOLOv10 model, which builds on earlier YOLO iterations, to increase the precision of rock melon leaf disease detection and classification. The technology lets farmers monitor crop health, raise yields, save labor expenses, and increase market earnings by incorporating AI. This work shows that YOLOv9 has better performance in terms of accuracy compared to YOLOv10; however, the processing time for the training process of YOLOv10 is faster than that of YOLOv9. This cutting-edge DL-based detection system offers a data-driven approach to disease management and useful solutions for enhancing the sustainability and production of rock melon farming using cutting-edge AI technology. It is a major advancement in smart agriculture.

articleTitle: A Coordinated Control Strategy for Flywheel Array Based on Moth-Flame Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: A proposed control technique aims to optimize the efficiency of the fly wheel array and maintain an energy balance for each unit in the flywheel array energy storage system. By integrating the improved Moth-Flame Optimization (MFO) technique with the goal of minimizing the power loss of the system, the study proposes a novel approach to dynamically allocate power based on the power command, thus optimizing overall system performance. This method not only reduces the energy disparity among flywheels but also enhances the lifespan and efficiency of the storage system. This prevents significant variations in residual energy among the flywheels while maintaining a high operating efficiency for t he array, incontrast tot he conventional flywheel array power allocation strategy. Ultimately, a simulation model is constructed using Matlab/Simulink to validate the accuracy of the technique.

articleTitle: Fabrication of PVA Hydrogel Coated 3D Printed PETG Optical Fiber for Biocompatible Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Dip coating is widely used in hydrogel based optical fiber. However, obtaining a uniform coating for microstructure such as optical fiber remains a challenge where its influence on the optical output is still scarce in literature. Dip coating parameters such as speed and viscosity of the solution will affect both the uniformity and thickness of the coating. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the optical output of optical fiber core coated with Polyvinyl Alcohol (PV A) hydrogel with varied dip coating speed (15, 30, 45, 60, 75 and 90 mm/min) and PVA concentrations (10, 15 and 20%). Firstly, the core of the optical fiber was self-fabricated using 3D printing technology, directly extruded from the commercially available Polyethylene Terephthalate Glycol-modified (PETG) filament. The uniformity and thickness of the coating were observed under optical microscope follows by analyses in ImageJ software to measure the thickness at four different points (top, bottom, left and right). The optical output is measured using 650 nm light source and measured using optical power meter. The results revealed that the higher the concentrations with high speed will results in a thicker coating compared with employing low concentrations at high speed. However, regardless of the speed and concentrations, all the coatings show non-concentricity which influence the optical output intensity. Optical power output shows that the higher optical output can be observed at high concentrations of 20% as it led to thicker coating regardless of the different speeds compared 10% PVA concentrations. Despite the non-uniform coating, the optical output of all the coated fiber shows improvement compared to non-coated fiber

articleTitle: Improving Reliability and Performance of Screen Printed Carbon Electrodes in Electrochemical Immunosensors
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Screen-printed electrodes (SPEs) have gained popularity in the electrochemical field due to their adaptability, repeatability, sensitivity, and suitability for point-of-care testing (POCT). Several parameters including electrolyte composition, scan rates, electrode material, analyte concentration, potential window, and temperature can affect the electrochemical activity when using cyclic voltammetry (CV). In this study, we focused on three parameters such as scan rates and electrolyte composition to enhance the screen-printed carbon electrodes (SPCEs) using CV. Five types of scan rates were introduced including 50 mVs<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, 100 mVs<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, 150 mVs<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, 200 mVS<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, and 250 mVs<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. As increased scan rates, the peak current and separation increase leads to changes in kinetic that may affect the electrode surface sensitivity. At 50 mVs<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, highlight how the analyte reacts on the surface of SPCE through a diffusion-controlled process. In addition, the electrolyte composition and the choice of electrolyte can impact ion availability, which affects the electrochemical reaction. In this study, 1 mM ferrocene carboxylic acid (FCA) and 1 mM ferrocyanide redox probe were compared for their electrolyte compositions. The 1 mM ferricyanide/ferrocyanide ionic compound of 0.1M KCl improved the electrical signal quality based on regression analysis of 0.9792. Finally, optimization of analyte concentrations was carried out at 1 mM, 3 mM, and 5 mM. The difference concentrations influence the diffusion layer and the current response. However, this study discovered that 5 mM concentrations displayed an R squared of 0.9954 Therefore, optimizing the parameters is crucial for achieving accurate, sensitive, and reproducible results. Understanding their influence on the electrode surface and the electrochemical response can help tailor the experimental conditions to specific conditions or research goals.

articleTitle: Exploratory Data Analysis for Malaysian Cases of Covid-19
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Risk factor analysis is essential in medical research and patient care, offering insights into the determinants of mortality and severe outcomes. It aids healthcare providers in improving patient management, tailoring interventions, and optimizing resource allocation. The COVID-19 pandemic underscored the importance of rapid and collaborative risk factor analysis. Machine learning (ML) algorithms have emerged as powerful tools for predicting risk factors, but they require thorough data cleaning and preparation. This paper focuses on the exploratory data analysis (EDA) of Malaysian COVID-19 cases to identify feasible variables for subsequent risk factor analysis, enhancing the precision and effectiveness of ML models in healthcare. In this study, data from 128 records from Hospital Sg Buloh were analyzed, focusing on 34 variables. The process involved data cleaning and various analytical techniques, including univariate, bivariate, and multivariate analyses. This exploratory data analysis (EDA) is crucial as it facilitates the identification and extraction of significant features for machine learning algorithms. EDA helps in understanding data patterns, relationships, and structures, ensuring that the resulting ML models are precise and effective. By thoroughly analyzing the data, EDA lays the foundation for robust risk factor analysis, ultimately enhancing decision-making and patient care in healthcare settings.

articleTitle: Precise Leg Abduction Hydrotherapy Exercise Pose Analysis for Real Time Monitoring and Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel technique for obtaining precise leg abduction hydrotherapy pose analysis in real-time. It aims to enhance hydrotherapy through the application of AI-powered pose estimation technology. The proposed system addresses the limitations of traditional subjective assessments by providing precise, real-time monitoring of gait and posture using computer vision techniques. The system tracks movements under-water using YOLO-NAS Pose, offering immediate feedback. The methodology involves capturing underwater movements with a high degree of accuracy, processing these movements to calculate precise joint angles, counting repetitions, and providing real-time insights. The experiments focused on a single exercise, leg abduction, performed by one individual. The results showed a joint extraction accuracy rate of 98.3%. Additionally, during live webcam testing on land, the system achieved an average frame rate of 4 frames per second (fps). These results highlight the system's potential to significantly improve the effectiveness of hydrotherapy rehabilitation by offering precise and real time feedback.

articleTitle: Near-Infrared Based Non-Invasive Glucose Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Diabetes is a worldwide health hazard that requires frequent testing due to its high blood glucose levels. Conventional fingerstick testing lacks the capacity for continuous monitoring, is painful, and produces biomedical waste. Promising substitutes include non- invasive glucometers that rely on optical technologies, particularly, Near-Infrared Spectroscopy (NIRS). Although there are some difficulties such as low signal-to- noise ratio and calibration issues, NIR- based sensors have promise for precise glucose prediction. The importance of NIR technology in developing non- invasive glucose sensing is highlighted in this paper. The main goal of ongoing research is to improve the reliability and feasibility of non- invasive glucose measurements which are essential for managing diabetes effectively.

articleTitle: Prediction Model Using Deep Learning for Lung Illness Severity Among Covid-19 Patients in Iraq
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (Covid-19) has had significant social, medical and economic impacts worldwide. Covid-19 causes lung infections, and QRT-PCR is an essential tool used to detect Covid-19 infection. However, QRT-PCR is insufficient to detect the severity of the disease and its impact on the lung. The aim of this paper is to determine the severity level of Covid-19 by studying lung CT scans of people diagnosed with the virus in Iraq. Accurate classification of lung lesions in patients with Covid-19 is a critical challenge. ResNet50 was chosen as the base model. A large dataset containing 560 CT images was collected. Salt and pepper noise was implemented to test the algorithm's ability to handle degraded and distorted data and then removed by Median Filter to improve the data where the affected area was extracted and identified before training from each image by segmentation technique (OTSU threshold) to measure the damage inside the lung. CT images obtained from Babylon Hospital in Iraq were used. A deep learning algorithm was used to predict the severity of lung disease in Covid-19 patients. The model outperformed the rest of the models when compared with the results. The results showed that the prediction accuracy for the training data was 95.6% and the validation accuracy was 94.9%. The accuracy for the rest of the models VGG16, DenseNet121, MobileNetV2, EfficientNetB0 was 91%, 90%, 91%, 92.3%, 92%, respectively.

articleTitle: Feasibility Analysis of PPE Detection Via YOLOv7 & YOLOv7-Pose to Enhance Workplace Safety
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Ensuring workplace safety in Pre-Fabrication environments is important, particularly in adhering to safety compliance protocols through the correct usage of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE). However, existing systems often fall short in detecting whether PPE is correctly worn or not, posing a risk to workplace safety. By creating a specialized dataset for Pre-Fabrication environments, the system can detect four PPE tools which are hard hat, glove, safety shoes and welding mask. The dataset contains 934 training images and 255 images for testing and validation, respectively. After rigorous training, testing and validation process, the experimental result and performance evaluation show that the PPE detection model achieved 96.8% precision, 95% recall and a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 0.879. However, with the current model, there are several false positive errors from the result where the model falsely detects other objects as PPE. Therefore, this study proposes a dual-model system employing YOLOv7 object detection and pose estimation models to further improve the accuracy of the PPE detection model and reduce false positives. This dual-model system, validated through live CCTV footage, provides a comprehensive solution for enhancing safety protocols in Pre-Fabrication workspaces.

articleTitle: An Efficient Frequency Guided Image Enhancement Network for Shadow Removal
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Shadow removal poses a significant challenge in computer vision as it seeks to accurately restore image details obscured by shadowed areas. Existing methods for shadow removal often struggle to strike a balance between computational complexity, speed, and performance, rendering many models either too resource-intensive or inadequately effective for realworld applications. Recognizing this gap, we introduce a novel Frequency Guided Network that integrates the benefits of frequency domain processing using Discrete Wavelet Transform with the benefits of deep learning. By decomposing input signals into low and high frequencies, our approach enables the network to prioritize the recovery of crucial information from low-frequency regions while preserving essential high-frequency details, which risk getting lost in the deeper network layers. Notably, our model exhibits impressive efficiency, with a mere parameter count of less than half a million while rivaling the performance of models with significantly more parameters - up to 200 times in some cases. This architecture allows us to process a 1024x1024 image in just 0.14s, demonstrating it's suitability for real world scenarios.

articleTitle: IoT-Sustainability Protection: Water Level Monitoring with Micro Leak Detection and Automatic Water Restoration
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)

authors.preferredName: Nik Nor Muhammad Saifudin Nik Mohd Kamal
authors.firstName: Nik Nor Muhammad Saifudin Nik Mohd

abstract: Efficient water resource management stands as a linchpin for sustainable development initiatives worldwide. To this end, this work endeavours to pioneer a comprehensive water level monitoring system with a focus on leak detection and automatic water restoration. Tailored with specialized sensors with cutting-edge automation technology to monitor water levels against predefined thresholds, promptly triggering restoration processes when necessary and identifying leaks in real-time. Central idea of the design is the incorporation of a dedicated rain sensor module, bolstering the micro leak detection capabilities while an ultrasonic sensor ensures precise measurement of water levels in tanks. In the event of a detected leak, rain sensor promptly initiates a signal, process by the main board which also known as the “brain” of the system and triggers an automatic cessation of water input to prevent wastage. Moreover, the system ensures seamless data logging by uploading pertinent information to a dedicated IoT cloud database, facilitating comprehensive monitoring and analysis. This innovative solution underscores not only its viability but also its practical efficacy, showcasing its potential to optimize water utilization and conservation efforts. Specifically, it excels in detecting micro droplets indicative of leaks in the tank. This work aims to spearhead the development of an advanced water level monitoring system, leveraging state-of-the-art of Arduino hardware and a diverse array of sensors, including ultrasonic and rain sensors as well as presenting a holistic framework poised to revolutionize water management practices.

articleTitle: Adaptive Retransmission for Wireless Sensor Nodes Under Bursty Error Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Wireless sensor nodes, used in disaster management and industrial applications, typically require high reliability and low energy consumption. This reliability is often hindered due to bursty channel errors in practical wireless systems. The existing retransmission scheme used in IEEE 802.15.4 fails to capture the characteristics of burst channels as they are designed under the assumption of uniform error channels. Thus, they do not significantly improve the reliability under bursty channels while increasing the energy consumption with multiple retransmissions. Our proposed method utilises Reinforcement Learning (RL) to develop an adaptive retransmission strategy. This strategy is informed by analysing the transmission history of the sensor. The RL algorithm learns the optimal policy, which maximises energy efficiency and Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR) in networks with burst channel errors. Our RL retransmission strategy performed better in PDR and energy efficiency than the IEEE 802.15.4 and Retransmission Adaptive Intelligence Medium Access Control (RAI-MAC) proposed in the literature. By adaptively modifying the retransmission strategy, we improved the energy efficiency and PDR by 16% and 10%, respectively, under a 10-15% packet error rate. The results highlight the importance of an adaptive retransmission strategy for resource-constrained wireless sensors.

articleTitle: Mitigating Racial Algorithmic Bias in Healthcare Artificial Intelligent Systems: A Fairness-Aware Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Racial bias in artificial intelligent (AI) systems is a pervasive problem that undermines fairness and perpetuates inequality. This paper presents an analysis of bias-mitigating algorithms applied to standard machine learning classifiers with the goal of reducing racial bias in healthcare access. The study integrates Reweighing, Adversarial Debiasing, and Exponentiated Gradient (with demographic parity) methods with two base classifiers: Logistic Regression and Random Forest Classifier. The evaluation framework employs both traditional predictive performance metrics—accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score—and fairness metrics, including average odds difference, disparate impact score, equal opportunity difference, and balanced accuracy. The study finds that after the application of bias-mitigating algorithms, the Random Forest Classifier augmented with the Reweighing algorithm is the superior model, achieving an accuracy of 88.01%, precision of 89%, recall of 97%, and F1 score of 93%, while also demonstrating a balance with respect to fairness. This indicates the model's capability to maintain equity across diverse racial groups and the Random Forest Classifier model's compatibility with the Reweighing technique. The model was then interpreted using Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations to offer clear insights into the decision-making process. By highlighting effective strategies for mitigating racial algorithmic bias and fostering interpretability, this paper contributes foundational knowledge crucial for ethical AI development in the healthcare sector.

articleTitle: EfficientNet-Based Deep Learning Neural Network for Accurate Plant Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: This paper presents a deep learning-based approach for the accurate detection of plant diseases utilizing the EfficientNetB0 convolutional neural network architecture. The study emphasizes the critical importance of early and precise identification of plant diseases in maintaining global food security and sustainable agricultural practices. The proposed model demonstrates superior performance in classifying plant diseases, achieving an accuracy of 99.65% on the New Plant Diseases Dataset, which comprises 87,000 images across 38 categories. The model architecture leverages advanced neural network layers, including Global Average Pooling 2D and Dense with SoftMax activation, to enhance feature extraction and classification accuracy. The research highlights the advantages of using the EfficientNetB0 model, which balances accuracy and computational efficiency, making it a viable tool for real-world agricultural applications. The study's findings contribute to the ongoing efforts to integrate artificial intelligence in agriculture, providing farmers with reliable tools for early disease detection and improved crop management.

articleTitle: Detecting Plant Stress and Phenotyping in Live California Crops Using Thermal Imaging Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: The timely detection of plant stress is crucial in modern agriculture, yet there remains a lack of practical efficient stress detection solutions. This paper presents a systematic study of plant stress detection in living plant leaves using the thermal image technique, particularly focusing on early detection of plant stress before visual stress symptoms appear. The most commonly studied types of plant stress include these three: drought, disease, and malnutrition in the plants. The nine types of plants studied were selected based on the prevalence in California crop acreage and yields: cucumber, strawberry, tomato, aloe vera, lettuce, dinosaur kale, grape, curly kale, and broccoli. Three areas were selected for each plant to represent stress levels. No stress (healthy) area, early-stressed area, and late-stressed area. Twenty temperature spots were collected within each area, and statistical analysis was applied for data analysis. The p-value of the healthy area compared to the early-stressed area on the strawberry is 0.036, and the p-value from the early-stress to late-stress is 0.038. The result indicates the thermal imaging technique is a sensitive method to detect plant stress caused by drought, disease, and malnutrition stress. In addition, to better predict plant stress development, drought stress models were built based on the phenotype characteristics of the tomato plant. The model will be applied to a thermal imaging drone on a larger scale to guide farmers for more efficient irrigation scheduling. The significance of this study is that it provides a practical method of stress detection within plants and offers an advanced and non-invasive method for early detection of plant stress, promoting a much more sustainable agriculture.

articleTitle: A Semantically Robust Adversarial Training Domain Adaptation Method for Tuberculosis Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial for tuberculosis diagnosis from X-ray images, as it mitigates variations arising from different imaging conditions across hospitals, thereby enhancing the generalization capability and reliability of tuberculosis diagnostic models. Cycle-consistent adversarial training methods have shown promising results in medical image domain adaptation by learning domain-invariant feature representations. However, these approaches often fail to preserve critical diagnostic information, such as the presence of lesions, during the image translation process, leading to suboptimal diagnostic performance. To address this limitation, a semantically robust adversarial training domain adaptation (SRAT-DA) method is proposed that maintains semantic consistency while translating image styles across domains. Cycle-consistent adversarial training is extended by incorporating semantic constraints to retain clinically relevant information during image transformation. The approach is evaluated on domain adaptation tasks between the Shenzhen and TBX11K TB X-ray datasets. The promising results, achieving an average accuracy of 73.7%, sensitivity of 73.0%, and specificity of 74.1%, demonstrate the effectiveness in improving TB diagnosis under domain shift scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhancing Traffic System Object Detection with YOLOv8 Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: This study investigates the application of the YOLOv8 algorithm for enhanced object detection within traffic systems. Object detection, a crucial aspect of intelligent transportation systems, requires high accuracy and rapid processing for effective traffic monitoring and management. Previous approaches, including various versions of R-CNN and SSD, have offered trade-offs between speed, accuracy, and complexity. This paper explores YOLOv8's capabilities, highlighting its superior inference speed and accuracy improvements over its predecessors. The study leverages a rather novel dataset, focusing on optimizing model parameters to achieve high precision, recall, and F1 scores. Hyperparameters such as optimizer, batch size, epochs and learning rate have been tuned to improve the model's performance results. The optimized YOLOv8 obtained great results with high precision and accuracy. An evaluation of YOLOv8 against other prominent models like SSD, EfficientDet, and Faster R-CNN is conducted to underscore its suitability for real-time traffic monitoring applications. This study's findings can significantly contribute to the field of traffic detection and intelligent transportation systems.

articleTitle: Comparative Evaluation of Pose Estimation Models for Underwater Hydrotherapy Gait Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Hydrotherapy provides health advantages, such as reducing pain, enhancing blood circulation and easing symptoms. Making use of cutting edge motion capture technology, the detection of poses without markers has emerged as a tool for examining exercise patterns for hydrotherapy patients. This research assesses the effectiveness of four pose estimation models-OpenPose, MediaPipe Pose, AlphaPose and YOLOv7-in extracting and analyzing human gait pose specifically under challenging underwater conditions (i.e: camera positioning, complex backgrounds, underwater imaging issues, and the absence of head connections). A dedicated dataset of hydrotherapy movements was developed to evaluate model accuracy. Findings revealed that YOLOv7 and AlphaPose outperformed the other techniques. YOLOv7 achieved the highest accuracy in scenarios involving multiple participants, delivering near-perfect results for single-person exercises both on land and underwater. For four-person exercises underwater, AlphaPose had an average accuracy of 90.6%, while YOLOv7 slightly outperformed it with an accuracy of 93%.

articleTitle: A Forest Acoustics – Temporal Frequency Convolution Neural Network Model for Detecting Illegal Logging Activities in Forest
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Illegal logging has detrimental effects on the environment, including increased deforestation, which hampers carbon sequestration and leads to heightened carbon emissions. Consequently, there is an imperative to detect and prevent illegal logging to safeguard the environment. Detecting logging activities involves discerning complex environmental sounds. Environmental sounds such as forest acoustics are very complex given that they often have background noises such as wind making it difficult to classify them. This study concentrates on employing deep learning techniques for classifying forest acoustics, tackling the complexities inherent in environmental sounds. It specifically delves into temporal and frequency patterns of forest sounds, isolating sounds indicative of logging activities such as chainsaw sounds. The Temporal Frequency Convolution Neural Network model (TFCNN) is deployed to accurately recognize logging related acoustics while dealing with background noise during classification and data processing. The TFCNN model consists of two main branches, the harmonic spectrogram branch, and the percussive spectrogram branch. The outputs of both harmonic and percussive branches are concatenated to combine the information learnt from both. The model was trained using the FSC 22 dataset, which is tailored for forest - related analyses, making it an ideal choice. To tackle background noise during classification, attention mechanisms and feature representation techniques were employed. The model recorded an accuracy of 87%.

articleTitle: Implementation of Object Tracking Using YOLOv7 Pose Estimation for Human Activity Recognition in Fabrication Yard via CCTV Videos
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: A new dataset is created in a fabrication yard environment for human activity classification. YOLOv7 object detection model is used to identify 5 classes which are welding, grinding, standing, sitting and walking. Five experiments were conducted, and Experiment 5 achieved the highest mean Average Precision (mAP_ 0.5) of 0.621. The mAP@0.5 value is the most critical metric as it reflects the model's ability to balance precision and recall across all confidence thresholds. This higher mAP@0.5 suggests that Experiment 5's model is better at accurately identifying. However, YOLOv7 object detection posed limitation to differentiate classes for sitting, standing and walking. The implementation of pretrained models YOLOv7 Object Tracking and YOLOv7 Pose Estimation is done respectively with YOLOv7 Object Detection to improve the detections. The YOLOv7 Object Tracking showed significant improvement in the detections of standing and walking but had limitation for sitting. The YOLOv7 Pose Estimation which uses the heuristic method showed significant improvement in the detections of standing, sitting and walking compared to YOLOv7 Object Tracking.

articleTitle: A Bi-Lingual Counselling Chatbot Application for Support of Gender Based Violence Victims in Kenya
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Gender-based violence (GBV) remains one of the highest prevailing human rights violations globally, surpassing national, social, and economic boundaries. However, due to its nature, it is masked within a culture of silence and causes detrimental effects on the dignity, health, autonomy, and security of its victims. Technological approaches have been established to tackle GBV as intermediate and supplementary support for victims as part of UN-SDG 5. Conversational Agents such as Chomi, ChatPal, and Namubot have been developed for counselling GBV victims who struggle with disclosing their predicament to humans. The existing chatbots, however, are not fit for Kenyan victims because they utilize languages such as Swedish, Finnish, Isizulu, Setswana and Isixhosa in addition to incorporating referral services specific to their regions. This research addressed this gap by developing a chatbot application suitable for the Kenyan region for counselling GBV victims using both Kiswahili and English, the languages predominantly used in the country, and including contacts to referral services. The methodology utilized involved developing a chatbot application based on the Rasa open-source AI framework by training a model using a pre-processed counselling dataset. The performance of the model was evaluated using the NLU confidence score to determine the model's certainty in its intent identification and a confusion matrix was generated which resulted in 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> classification threshold accuracy for 80% training and 20% testing data split. Python's Fuzzy Matching Token Set Ratio score was also used to determine the response that best matches the input with results indicating satisfactory performance of the model ranging between 63% and 92% for GBV queries input. The developed model was then integrated into a web application as the user interface for user access and interaction with the model hence achieving the research objective of developing a chatbot application to conduct counselling for GBV victims in Kenya using English and Kiswahili languages.

Author Keywords: Fuzzy Matching Token Set Ratio score

articleTitle: Non-Contact Breathing Signal and Rate Estimation Based on EEMD Using IR-UWB
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Impulse Radio Ultra-Wideband (IR-UWB) radar technology has great promise for non-contact sensing applications, especially for detecting human vital signs like breathing rate (BR) and figuring out a person's range. A methodology for determining the breathing frequency and range of stationary sit-still individuals at four distinct ranges-1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex>, 1.5 m, 2 m, and 2.5 m-is shown in this work. The preprocessing methods suggested by the study include average subtraction and the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT). In order to determine the human BR in the frequency domain, the chosen bin is decomposed using Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (EEMD) and processed using the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). An X4M03 (IR-UWB) radar was used to collect data for the assessment of the approach, and Python software was used to handle the raw signals that were reflected. According to the experiment results, the subjects' accuracy was maximum at a range of 1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex>, scoring 93.07%.

articleTitle: Using Direct-Georeferencing with a MEMS-LiDAR to Classify Traffic Signs, an Automatic Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: In this article, a micro-electromechanical systems light-detection and ranging (MEMS-LiDAR) based sampling method for traffic sign recognition is presented. MEMS-LiDAR is an emerging remote-sensing technology in the autopilot (AP) area. Existing published scientific reports have been less concerned with using point-cloud datasets sampled from MEMS-LiDAR, as the MEMS-LiDAR is a recently matured commercial technology. In this paper, we propose utilizing a MEMS-LiDAR system (Robosense-M1) for data acquisition in a mobile laser scanning (MLS) in an urban environment. Subsequently, two methods related to clustering and point-cloud 3D geometric feature extraction are introduced to segment and filter out plain-like objects. Finally, a support vector machine method (SVM) is investigated for the task of traffic-sign classification. Our results successfully demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method with K1-score based on the MEMS-LiDAR sampled data to be 83.33%. This result shows the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Speaker Tracking Using Audio-Assisted Azure Kinect Body Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)

authors.preferredName: Muhammad Atiff Zakwan Bin Mohd Ariffin
Siti Nur Aisyah Binti Mohd Robi

abstract: Equipped with various sensors, such as a color camera, a depth camera, and microphone arrays, the Azure Kinect can potentially be used in multi-modal speaker tracking. By exploiting one of its features, Azure Kinect Body Tracking (AKBT), it can track multiple people simultaneously using the depth camera, thus beneficial for speaker-tracking-related activities. Therefore, we devise an experiment with varying scenarios, such as various speakers, occlusion between speakers, and movement within and outside of the camera's field of view (FOV), to test the tracking capabilities of AKBT (without audio). After that, we further improve the AKBT system by proposing an audio-assisted AKBT (A-AKBT), which combines the AKBT system with the Steered-Response Power with Phase Transform (SRP-PHAT) technique via an adaptive data fusion process. We compared the tracking performance using multiple object tracking accuracy (MOTA) and generalized optimal sub-pattern assignment (GOSPA) metrics. We discovered that the A-AKBT improves both metrics since it manages to recover missing tracking in some scenarios.

articleTitle: Improving Personal Protective Equipment Detection in Fabrication Yard Using Image Augmentation with YOLOv7
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Accurate object detection is crucial for industrial safety applications such as monitoring the safety of workers in an industrial location. This study examines the impact of applying data augmentation techniques in tandem with the YOLOv7 object detection model to identify three desired classes which are hard hats, safety shoes, and regular shoes. The utilized dataset is 2300 for training images, 400 for validation images, and 600 for test images, covering various scenarios from the industrial environment and general environment. Five experiments were conducted using different combinations of data augmentation methods which are: padding, flipping, resizing, and cropping. The experiment that applied padding, resizing, and flipping to the original 640×640 images achieved the highest mean Average Precision (mAP_0.5) of 0.8597. Another experiment, which combined multiple augmentations across different resolutions, including padding, flipping, resizing, and cropping, produced the second-highest mAP_0.5 of 0.8568. The baseline experiment without augmentation achieved a mAP_0.5 of 0.6412, while resizing images to 320×320 without other augmentations resulted in a slight decrease to 0.6296. An experiment combining resizing, cropping, and flipping on 320×320 images yielded a mAP_0.5 of 0.8323. Based on the results achieved, the augmentation techniques that were applied significantly enhanced the results achieved compared to the non-augmented baseline runs. The findings highlight the effectiveness of data augmentation in improving the generalization capabilities of object detection models by combining diverse augmentation methods like padding, resizing, and flipping proved to be the most effective combination thus suggesting a synergistic effect for the detection of hard hat, safety shoes and shoes.

articleTitle: Case Study in Urban Community Farming: IoT-Based Soil Moisture Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) technology has transformed every part of the lives of average people, making things easier. A network of independent devices is known as the Internet of Things (IoT). The aim of this project is to propose an Internet of Things (IoT)-based farming system that gives farmers access to real-time information on soil moisture level as well as surrounding temperature and humidity for efficient environmental monitoring. By using this method, farmers will be able to increase their total productivity and product quality and engage in smart farming practices. The smart farming system developed in this paper incorporated IoT technology and LoRaWAn communication protocol for long distance monitoring where Wi-Fi connection is unavailable. The system was also supplied by solar energy using solar panel integrated at the transmitter and receiver circuits. The RSSI and SNR levels were also measured at Line-of-Sight (LOS) test and during deployment at the urban community farm in Taman Sutera 2, Seberang Jaya, Pulau Pinang. The lowest Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) level recorded was −110 dBm at a LOS distance of 300 m between transmitter and receiver devices while the Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) recorded was at 5 dB. A 48-hours deployment testing at the farm was conducted and the results are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: A Systematic Literature Review of Multimodal Analysis Techniques for Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: As cyber threats continue to evolve in complexity, traditional malware detection methods often fall short in identifying sophisticated attacks. Multimodal analysis, which integrates various data sources and analytical methods, has emerged as a promising approach to enhance malware detection capabilities. This paper presents a systematic literature review (SLR) of existing research on multimodal analysis techniques for malware detection. We conducted an extensive search across two major databases and identified 31 studies that explore the multimodal approaches for malware detection. Our review synthesizes the methodologies, modalities, and evaluation metrics used in these studies, highlighting their strengths and limitations. The findings reveal that multimodal approaches significantly improve detection accuracy and robustness compared to single-modality methods. However, challenges such as data integration complexity, computational overhead, scalability, and transparency remain. This review also identifies research gaps and suggests directions for future work to further advance the field of malware detection.
